title: Russian ballistic missiles strike the centre of Sumy on Palm Sunday
body:
On 13 April 2025, which was Palm Sunday, two Russian ballistic missiles struck the centre of Sumy, a city in northeastern Ukraine. According to Ukraine's Defence Intelligence, the missiles were Iskander types fired by the 112th and 448th missile brigades from Voronezh and Kursk oblasts. The second strike hit about 200 metres from the first, in an area that included residential, educational and commercial buildings. Presidential Office head Andrii Yermak said the missiles carried cluster munitions.

Casualty figures rose during the day. Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported 34 dead and 117 injured as of 6 p.m. on 13 April, and the Sumy Oblast Prosecutor's Office later raised the death toll to 35. Oleh Strilka gave 119 injured, including 15 children, as of the morning of 14 April, and said 34 people were killed, including seven children. Authorities reported damage to 20 buildings, including four educational institutions, as well as cars, trams, cafes and shops.

President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the strikes and called for pressure on Russia. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called an attack on a major Christian holiday "absolute evil." US President Donald Trump said Russia "made a mistake." The strikes came one day after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on 12 April.
